subject: Strange errors with very simple model

messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Strange errors with very simple model
parts:
Hello,

Coming back to Stan after a long break.  Some things seem to have changed. (Or I've forgotten something obvious.)

I need to develop a hierarchical zero inflated Poisson regression model with about 20 covariates.  The plan was to start with a very simple Poisson regression, then build up the layers of complexity once that was working.

The problem is that I'm getting compilation errors on the most simple Poisson regression, so am missing something.  I simply want to have the coefficients of the model drawn from a multivariate normal distribution, then fit the Poisson model - the goal being to get a nice group of samples from the posterior for the coefficients. 

I could use some help on sorting this out.  Any and all feedback is welcome.

Thanks!

Below is my Stan code:

data{
    int<lower=0> N; // number of cases
    int<lower=0> P; // Number of covariates
    real<lower=0> y[N]; // Count for each case -> dependent variable
    matrix[N,P] X; // Covariates for model
}

parameters {
    vector[P] betas;
    cov_matrix[P] Sigma;
    real eta;
}

transformed parameters {

}

model {

    betas ~ multi_normal(0, Sigma);

    for(n in 1:N){   
        eta <- dot_product(X[n], betas);
        y[n] ~ poisson(eta);
    }   
}

messages.subject: Re: Strange errors with very simple model
parts:
On Monday, June 24, 2013 2:20:38 PM UTC-4, Noah wrote:
The problem is that I'm getting compilation errors on the most simple Poisson regression, so am missing something.
In general, if you have compilation problems, we need to see the output to diagnose it. However, in this case, ...

data{
    int<lower=0> N; // number of cases
    int<lower=0> P; // Number of covariates
    real<lower=0> y[N]; // Count for each case -> dependent variable
    matrix[N,P] X; // Covariates for model
}

the dependent variable needs to be integer valued, not real. Like

int<lower=0> y[N];

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Strange errors with very simple model
parts:
In the model block, just do

y ~ poisson_log(X * betas);

This will avoid the error, avoid the loop, and avoid an unnecessary logarithm inside the poisson log-likelihood. If you did poisson(exp(X * betas)), it would be the same mathematically but be slower and less numerically stable. You can find the relevant page in the Stan manual from the index of functions.

Ben

parts: If so, then you probably want to reconceptualize your N by P matrix as an N-array of row vectors of length P

data{
int<lower=0> N; // number of cases
int<lower=0> P; // Number of covariates
int<lower=0> y[N]; // Count for each case

row_vector[P] X[N]; // Covariates for model "like" a NxP matrix
}

Then I think that

for (n in 1:N) y[n] ~ poisson_log(dot_product(X[n], beta));

would work, although it is still better to use poisson_log() than poisson(exp()).

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Strange errors with very simple model
parts:
The problem isn't in the dot product syntax, but that
you are trying to assign a value to a parameter, which
Stan doesn't allow.

Variables can only be assigned in the block in which
they are declared, and there are no statements allowed
in a parameters block, so parameters can't be assigned to
anywhere. You can define eta as a transformed parameter
and assign to it in the transformed parameters block.

If you need something that can be assigned to, use a local
variable. For example, this is well formed, as would be
replacing "model" with "transformed parameters":

parameters {
matrix[3,2] A;
vector[2] B;
...
}
model {
real C;
C <- dot_product(A[1],B);
...
}

The only difference between transformed parameters and local variables
in the model block is that transformed parameters are returned along
with parameters as output by the sampler (or optimizer).

You can also declare A as an array of (row) vectors, which
is a bit more efficient as it doesn't require allocation and
copies (matrices are stored column-major, so you can't easily
slice out a row w/o a non-memory-local copy).

- Bob
